the cosmological data do not support the existence of a sterile neutrinos that mixes with the electron or muon neutrino.

the cosmological data from Planck and other surveys are not in tension with the LSND and/or MiniBooNE anomalies, and are not able to confirm them, but can rule out a large part of the LSND allowed region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cosmological data are not able to probe the sterile neutrinos at a level that is competitive with the current and upcoming particle physics experiments.
cosmological constraints on sterile-neutrino oscillations are competitive with those coming from particle physics experiments.

the sterile neutrino parameter space that is allowed by Planck and BAO is not compatible with the hints of the sterile neutrinos coming from some of the neutrino oscillation channels, but it is consistent with the hints from other oscillation channels, and the global fit of neutrino oscillation experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cosmological bounds are not as strong as previously thought.
cosmological data can constrain the sterile neutrino model parameters with different priors from the ones used in particle physics experiments.

the cosmological constraints on sterile-neutrino oscillations are competitive with the best laboratory constraints in the case where sterile neutrinos mix exclusively with muon and tau neutrinos, and that they will be competitive in the near future in the case where the sterile neutrinos only mix with electron neutrinos, if future CMB experiments reach their expected sensitivity.
